title: Quantile Headroom Orchestrator and Spillover Smoothing Adapter
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally hit transient utilization spikes that deterministic headroom policies either over-provision for or react to too late. This PR introduces a Quantile Headroom Orchestrator (QHO) that maintains headroom budgets using tail-aware quantiles derived from short and medium windows, and a Spillover Smoothing Adapter that gracefully redirects excess load to compatible fallback capacity tiers with controlled ramping. The change aims to reduce wasted reserved capacity while keeping throughput guarantees during short, heavy tails. Scope: - New controller implementing dual-window quantile estimation and safe headroom allocations. - Smoothing adapter that exposes a BufferAllowance signal to the scheduler and a SpilloverRamp policy to the fleet router. - Lightweight telemetry hooks, histograms and HDR sketches for per-pool quantile reporting. - API additions: small protobuf update to autoscaler.proto to surface QuantilePolicy and BufferAllowance. - New unit and e2e tests including synthetic spike scenarios and rollback safety checks. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + simulation results attached (linear ENG-3421) - [x] Unit tests for quantile estimator and allocator - [x] E2E spike test in perf-canary harness - [x] Telemetry dashboards (draft) - [x] Backward-compatible protobuf evolution Notes: This PR is intended to be non-breaking for existing resource configs; the default autoscaler policy remains unchanged unless QuantilePolicy is enabled on a pool. See linked Linear tickets for tuning knobs and simulation traces: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3421/quantile-headroom-orchestrator and relatedSUP ticket SUP-9123 for customer incident context.

review_comments: Marco Li: Can you explain why we need dual windows vs exponential decay? The simulator shows better tail sensitivity but we need explanation in comments.

Asha Patel: Dual windows separate short spikes from sustained drift. Short window picks up microbursts; medium window prevents thrashing when traffic trends. Added inline comment and updated design doc.
Sofia Nguyen: Telemetry looks good; please add the per-pool 99.9th quantile to the allocation UI so SREs can observe headroom pressure.
Asha Patel: Added hdr sketch exporter and a dashboard JSON draft under docs/; left follow-up (ENG-3478) to iterate on UI surface.
Ethan Brooks: Integration tests flaky on arm64 CI (timing-sensitive). Suggest using deterministic clocks or increased tolerances in e2e.
Asha Patel: Replaced a time.Sleep with a controlled clock in tests and increased tolerances where simulation variance was expected.
Marco Li: Approved after small nits fixed (comments and a logging level adjustment).
release_notes:
- Introduce Quantile Headroom Orchestrator: tail-aware headroom allocations to reduce over-reservation and improve responsiveness to microbursts.
- Add Spillover Smoothing Adapter: controlled redirection to fallback capacity with ramp policies to preserve throughput guarantees.
- New telemetry: per-pool HDR sketches and quantile exports for monitoring headroom pressure.
post_merge_actions: deploy-canary: enable QuantilePolicy on a single dedicated pool in perf-canary
monitoring: add dashboard panels to dedicated-capacity -> headroom view
follow-up: ENG-3478 to expose BufferAllowance in Console UI
notes_for_backport: Low-risk for backporting to release/2026-Q1: protobuf is additive and defaults to current behavior. If backporting, ensure the hdrsketch dependency is available in the release branch.
incident_reference: SUP-9123: customer reported sudden sustained tail spikes causing transient SLA violations; QHO was simulated for mitigation and this PR implements the solution.
